citation: Nemhauser, Wolsey, Fisher (1978). An analysis of approximations for maximizing submodular set functions - I
problem: Cardinality-constrained maximization of monotone submodular set functions
method: Worst-case analysis of greedy and interchange heuristics; (1-1/e) approximation guarantee for greedy under monotone submodularity
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Canonical justification for greedy/fixed-ranking placement: greedy is near-optimal only when the objective is monotone submodular
exact_remaining_gap: Guarantee is void when the objective is neither submodular nor supermodular (our alpha(S) has discrete second differences of both signs); says nothing about small-signal stability margins

citation: Lovász (1983). Submodular functions and convexity
venue: In: Mathematical Programming The State of the Art, Springer Berlin Heidelberg, pp. 235-257
problem: Structural link between submodular set functions and convex functions
method: Lovász extension: a set function is submodular iff its extension is convex; polyhedral characterization
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Provides the formal definition/test (non-positive vs non-negative second differences) we apply to alpha(S)
exact_remaining_gap: Pure theory; no power-system or eigenvalue objective

citation: Topkis (1978). Minimizing a submodular function on a lattice
problem: Conditions under which optimal solutions of parametric problems are monotone (isotone) in the parameter; submodular minimization on lattices
method: Lattice-theoretic analysis; increasing differences / submodularity implies monotone comparative statics
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Explains when a fixed (context-free) ordering of choices can be optimal (consistent-sign differences); our sign-mixed second differences violate this premise
exact_remaining_gap: No dynamic-system or stability application

citation: Topkis (1998). Supermodularity and complementarity
venue: Princeton University Press (Frontiers of Economic Research)
problem: Theory of supermodularity, complementarity and monotone comparative statics
method: Book-length treatment of supermodular functions on lattices, increasing differences, and monotone optimal solutions
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Standard reference for complementarity (supermodular) vs substitutability (submodular) between elements; our SG->GFL replacements act as complements in some contexts and substitutes in others
exact_remaining_gap: No power-system content

citation: Fujishige (2005). Submodular functions and optimization (2nd ed.)
venue: Annals of Discrete Mathematics, Vol. 58, Elsevier
problem: Comprehensive theory of submodular systems, base polyhedra and submodular optimization
method: Monograph (2nd ed. adds submodular function minimization and discrete convex analysis chapters)
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Standard reference for definitions and algorithms of submodular optimization
exact_remaining_gap: No power-system content

citation: Bach (2013). Learning with submodular functions: a convex optimization perspective
venue: Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 6(2-3):145-373
problem: Submodular function theory and optimization from a convex-analysis viewpoint
method: Lovász extension, polyhedra, submodular minimization/maximization algorithms; applications incl. sensor placement and subset selection
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Accessible modern reference for testing/exploiting submodularity in placement problems
exact_remaining_gap: No stability-margin objectives; no treatment of set functions with mixed-sign curvature arising from dynamics

citation: Summers, Cortesi, Lygeros (2016). On submodularity and controllability in complex dynamical networks
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems 3(1):91-101 (Corrections: TCNS 5(3):1503, 2018, doi 10.1109/TCNS.2017.2670506)
problem: Actuator/sensor placement maximizing Gramian-based controllability/observability metrics
method: Shows several Gramian metrics are modular or submodular set functions; greedy placement; example of power-electronic actuator placement in a European grid model. A published correction (2018) amends part of the submodularity claims (cf. Olshevsky 2018)
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Closest control-theory precedent for treating a placement set function on a linear dynamical network; power-grid example
exact_remaining_gap: Metrics are Gramian energy measures of a fixed linear model, not the rightmost eigenvalue of a re-linearized system after re-solving equilibrium; no SG->GFL replacement, no sign reversal of marginal effects; the correction shows submodularity claims are fragile

citation: Olshevsky (2018). On (non)supermodularity of average control energy
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems 5(3):1177-1181
problem: Whether average control energy (trace of inverse Gramian) is supermodular in the actuated set
method: Proof that the function is not necessarily supermodular, correcting prior literature
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Precedent that natural dynamic performance set functions can fail modularity assumptions; supports our non-sub/non-supermodularity finding
exact_remaining_gap: Energy metric, not an eigenvalue stability margin; no power-system equilibrium re-solution, no IBR replacement, no quantification of greedy/fixed-ranking failure rates

citation: Summers, Kamgarpour (2019). Performance guarantees for greedy maximization of non-submodular controllability metrics
problem: Greedy actuator/sensor selection when Gramian metrics (e.g., minimum eigenvalue) are not submodular
method: Bounds via submodularity ratio and curvature for non-submodular set functions
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Directly addresses greedy selection when submodularity fails; submodularity ratio/curvature are natural diagnostics for our alpha(S)
exact_remaining_gap: Conference paper; Gramian metrics, not rightmost eigenvalue; no SG->GFL replacement, no controller-policy dependence, no evidence of sign reversal of marginal gains

citation: Qin, Yang, Rajagopal (2019). Submodularity of storage placement optimization in power networks
problem: Placement of energy storage in a power network with optimal storage control to minimize system cost
method: Duality/polyhedral analysis of parametric economic dispatch; tight condition for submodularity of placement value; modified greedy (1-1/e) when verified; risk-aware extension
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Power-system placement set function whose submodularity is condition-dependent (spatiotemporal congestion pattern critical), i.e., structure depends on operating context
exact_remaining_gap: Economic (cost) objective with steady-state dispatch; no small-signal dynamics, no IBR/SG replacement or controller gains

citation: Liu, Clark, Bushnell et al. (2019). Controlled islanding via weak submodularity
problem: Selecting transmission lines to trip for controlled islanding (generator non-coherency + load-generation imbalance)

exact_remaining_gap: Line-set islanding objective, not small-signal eigenvalue under SG->GFL replacement; no test of sign-mixed second differences or fixed-ranking failure

citation: Yang, Huang, Xin et al. (2021). Placing grid-forming converters to enhance small signal stability of PLL-integrated power systems
problem: Where to place GFM converters (switch PLL-based GFL units to GFM) to improve PLL-induced small-signal stability

topology: modified two-area system; nine converters on IEEE 39-bus network
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Same network (IEEE 39-bus) and combinatorial choice of which units change control mode; greedy sequential placement
exact_remaining_gap: Grid-strength (Laplacian eigenvalue) surrogate; no SG->GFL replacement, no nested-portfolio marginal sign reversal, no submodularity test, no quantification of fixed-ranking failure

citation: Xin, Liu, Chen et al. (2025). How many grid-forming converters do we need? A perspective from small signal stability and power grid strength
problem: Required GFM/GFL capacity ratio to reach a prescribed small-signal stability margin
method: Admittance-model comparison of GFL vs GFM voltage-source behavior; gSCR shown linear in GFM capacity ratio under identical ratios and homogeneous GFL wind farms; high-fidelity simulations

exact_remaining_gap: Homogeneity/identical-ratio assumptions make the effect monotone and context-free; no SG retirement, no node-specific marginal effects or sign reversal, no set-function structure

citation: Zhang, Chen, Chen et al. (2026). Small-signal stability and inertia constrained optimal configuration method of grid-forming energy storage systems
problem: Optimal placement and capacity of GFM energy storage under small-signal stability and inertia constraints

exact_remaining_gap: Adds GFM ESS rather than replacing SGs with GFL; abstract reports no marginal-effect sign reversal, no submodularity analysis, no AVR/Q-V gain dependence study (only abstract verified)

citation: Lamrani, Cardozo, Prevost et al. (2027). Placing grid-forming controlled converters to enhance power system small-signal stability
problem: Placement of GFM-controlled converters for small-signal stability of transmission grids

closest_overlap_with_our_work: Recent iterative (sequential) GFM placement for small-signal stability
exact_remaining_gap: Content of journal version not verified; no evidence found of SG->GFL replacement sign reversal, submodularity test, or fixed-ranking evaluation

citation: Poolla, Groß, Dörfler (2019). Placement and implementation of grid-forming and grid-following virtual inertia and fast frequency response

closest_overlap_with_our_work: Placement of GFM vs GFL devices; optimal allocation depends on implementation (GFM vs GFL)
exact_remaining_gap: Continuous allocation of inertia/damping gains with H2 (frequency) objective, not discrete SG->GFL replacement with rightmost-eigenvalue margin; no set-function curvature analysis

citation: Markovic, Stanojev, Aristidou et al. (2021). Understanding small-signal stability of low-inertia systems
problem: Maximum permissible IBR penetration and unstable-mode nature under different SG/GFM/GFL generation portfolios

closest_overlap_with_our_work: Shows stability depends on generation portfolio and unit placement, not only aggregate IBR share (one scenario stable at 78.5% GFL while another unstable at 62%); removing one of two GFM units destabilizes
exact_remaining_gap: Scenario-based penetration limits; does not isolate the marginal effect of the same SG->GFL replacement across nested portfolios, test sub/supermodularity, or evaluate fixed rankings

citation: Stanojev, Markovic, Aristidou et al. (2023). Improving stability of low-inertia systems using virtual induction machine synchronization for grid-following converters

closest_overlap_with_our_work: Closest setup: nested SG->GFL replacement on IEEE 39-bus with the stable range depending on GFL synchronization policy (PLL up to about 70%, VIM up to about 85%); authors remark that percentages change slightly with different permutations of the portfolio
exact_remaining_gap: Single fixed replacement order; permutation dependence only remarked, not quantified; no marginal eigenvalue shifts, sign reversal, set-function curvature or ranking analysis (39-bus details read from arXiv v2, June 2022)

citation: Li, Green, Gu (2023). The intrinsic communication in power systems: a new perspective to understand synchronization stability
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers 70(11):4615-4626
problem: Synchronization stability of mixed voltage-source (SG/GFM) and current-source (GFL) grids
method: Power-communication isomorphism; critical eigenvalue of a network-apparatus matrix; participation analysis; EMT simulation
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Reports a context-dependent sign flip: 100% GFL grid stable, adding one SG destabilizes it, adding further SGs at influential nodes restores stability (marginal effect of the same unit type depends on the existing portfolio)
exact_remaining_gap: Five hand-picked cases on 68-bus; adds SGs to a GFL grid rather than SG->GFL retirement; no systematic nested-portfolio marginals, set-function curvature, or ranking evaluation (case details read from arXiv v4, March 2023)

citation: Gautam, Vittal, Harbour (2009). Impact of increased penetration of DFIG-based wind turbine generators on transient and small signal stability of power systems

exact_remaining_gap: Sign is mode-dependent via inertia sensitivity, not shown to depend on the existing portfolio; DFIG era; no nested portfolios, set-function analysis or ranking

citation: Dong, Xin, Wu et al. (2019). Small signal stability analysis of multi-infeed power electronic systems based on grid strength assessment

exact_remaining_gap: Homogeneous-device reduction gives a context-free, monotone index; no SGs retired, no marginal sign reversal, no set-function/ranking analysis

citation: Coletta, Jacquod (2016). Linear stability and the Braess paradox in coupled-oscillator networks and electric power grids

method: Linear stability analysis of coupled-oscillator and power-grid models; analysis of the added edge
